page: Microsoft Azure D8s_v3 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DSv3 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon E5-2673 v4 processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The instance is configured with 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It includes 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, alongside 66 GB of local storage and capability for Premium Storage.

Performance benchmarks indicate that the D8s_v3 is positioned in the lower tiers for single-core execution and memory throughput. The single-core stress-ng and Geekbench scores fall into the weak and poor categories, respectively, reflecting the older Broadwell-generation CPU architecture. Memory bandwidth tests for both small and large blocks also register in the bottom 25%. However, multi-core performance is more resilient, with stress-ng multi-core and Passmark memory scores reaching the average tier. Additionally, LLM inference speed for prompt processing and text generation using a small 135M model achieves average-tier performance.

The primary tradeoff of the D8s_v3 is its lower single-threaded processing speed and restricted memory bandwidth, which limits its utility for high-performance computing or intensive database operations. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated CPU allocation and balanced resource density make it a stable option for workloads that benefit from multi-threading rather than raw single-core speed. It is suited for general-purpose workloads, moderate web serving, small-scale model inference, and legacy applications that require Premium Storage compatibility without demanding modern CPU instruction sets like AVX-512.
